Anuj: Quick q about the /reorder endpoint contract — tie-breaking semantics? Clients (search + recommendations) depend on deterministic order when scores tie. Are we guaranteeing stable (input) order, or should we define an explicit tie-breaker?

Mel: The design doc said 'stable by input order within a response'. I don't think that's encoded in the OpenAPI yet. Good to lock it down.

Kevin: We currently return in-score-desc then preserve input order (stable sort) as an implementation detail. But that isn't promised across model or runtime versions.

Anuj: Two follow-ups: 1) Can we add an explicit field to the request to let callers pick tie-break behavior (e.g. input_index | item_id | random)? 2) How should we treat missing/null/NaN scores in ranking responses?

Mel: Adding an optional enum is backward-compatible if the default keeps current behavior. For missing scores: better to unify server-side behavior: treat missing as -Inf (i.e., put last) rather than error, unless client asks for strict validation.

TJ: Suggestion: request payload could accept "tie_break": "input_index" (default). Also offer "tie_seed" for reproducible random tie-break when tie_break=random. Example request: 
```json
{
  "items": [{"id":"A","payload":{}},{"id":"B","payload":{}}],
  "tie_break": "input_index"
}
```

Kevin: I'm wary of introducing random as a default — that can cause flaky ordering in downstream dedupe. If we provide random, require an explicit seed. Also prefer server normalize NaN -> error 400, missing -> -Inf.

Anuj: That sounds reasonable. So proposed contract: 
- score: optional per-item. If missing -> treated as -Inf for ranking.
- NaN/Infinity -> validation error (400) unless client supplies "lenient_scores": true.
- "tie_break": optional enum ["input_index","item_id","random"], default "input_index". If "random" then optional "tie_seed" integer for deterministic behavior.

Mel: Please add this to OpenAPI + docs. Call out that order is only stable within a single API response — we do not promise stable ordering across model upgrades or backend changes. Add an example in the migration guide.

Anuj: Will do. I'll open a PR with the OpenAPI change and example tests for tie cases. Assigning reviewers @Mel and @Kevin.

ops-bot: CI: ran unit tests for branch feature/reorder-tiebreak — all checks passed :white_check_mark:

Kevin: Quick nit — include an example for client SDKs showing how to pass "tie_seed" for reproducible results, and update the Go/TS SDKs to expose the enum.

TJ: Also add an integration test that sends 100 identical-score items and ensures ordering matches requested tie-break for each strategy.

Anuj: Great notes — PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234 — draft created. I'll add the change log entry and integration tests next.

Mel: I'll review tomorrow morning and leave comments. Thanks for pushing this, Anuj. :+1:
